every: all the people, things, times, etc.
I work every day from 6:00 to 9:30.
evidence: Evidence is facts or observations that support an idea.
The gun is evidence that professor Pickle killed Mr. Mustard.
In a courtroom, evidence refers to anything that is shown to the judge that is related to the case during a trial.
When you evidence something, you provide evidence or the truth of an event.
Something good must have happened to her, as evidenced by the smile on her face.
evaluation: Evaluation is the process of making a judgement.
If a teacher doesn't know the student well, it makes the evaluation of the student's level very difficult.
Lamont Library’s 24-hour service received a positive evaluation this past spring.
evaluate: If you evaluate someone or something, you judge it.
It is difficult to evaluate the effectiveness of the LINK programme, but we believe it has been useful.
even: You use even to focus on the most surprising or unlikely case.
Even in peaceful countries, there are problems.
Everyone walks to school here, even the teachers.
She didn't tell me about it and I expect she wasn't even aware of it.
Our progress was not rewarded. In fact, it was not even mentioned.
He won't lose his job, not even temporarily.
I hid it in the books where nobody would look. Even so, I worried about it all evening.
If things are even, the top or surface of each is as high as the others.
The top of the wall is even because the bricks are all the same size.
If a number is even, it can be divided into 2 equal parts.
2, 4, 6 and 8 are even numbers. 1, 3, 5 and 7 are not even numbers; they are odd numbers.
If you even something (out/up), you reduce the ups and downs; you make it smooth or equal.
India was leading 2-1, but Australia evened the score in the last minute.
If you even a problem out, you solve it.
I went down and evened it all out. Everyone's happy now.
ever: If I ask you if you have ever been to France, I am asking if you have been to France at any time in your life.
Have you ever met a king or queen?
I will love you forever and ever.
evolution: Evolution is the process of slow change. It is most used in biology to refer to the way living things change over long periods of time in order to adapt to their surroundings.
The theory of evolution is the basis of modern biology.
An evolution is a change that happens over time.
Over the last ten years, there has been an evolution in the way we think about this disease.
event: An event is anything that happens.
The event of her walking into the room happened before the event of the book falling off the table, so she saw it fall.
An event is when many people come together at a time they choose for a reason or for fun.
At the event tomorrow we're going to have balloons and music.
eventually: If something will happen eventually, it will happen but it will be in the future, not soon. Some day it will happen.
I'll clean out my closet eventually.
evitable: When something is evitable, it can be avoided.
evening: We eat a big meal in the evening.
everyday: something that is done a lot or happens a lot; something that is ordinary
evil: The opposite of good, if something is evil it is very far from good or is against good. This usually means in a way that is not moral or not ethical.
Hitler was a very evil person.
The quality of being evil; evilness.
He was so full of evil I do not think he knew what good was.
Something that causes harm, or harm itself.
We faced many evils on our journey.
The source or cause of evil as a spiritual or supernatural force. This is often called true evil.
I have seen things that lead me to believe that real evil exists.
evilness: The quality of being evil. If you have evilness you behave badly.
everything: Everything is all that exists, or all things in one area.
If you win, you get everything: the car and all other prizes you won!
everywhere: I've looked everywhere else, so it must be here.
evergreen: An evergreen is a tree that stays green all year.
The pine tree is an evergreen.
eventual: An eventual win, return, death, etc. is one that happens after a long time.
She joined a law firm with the eventual goal of working for government.
evolve: If something evolves, it, or things of its kind, change slowly over a long time or from generation to generation.
Because computer technology evolves rapidly, a product may have changed before most people learn about it.
evict: If you evict someone, you take their home from them.
The council evicted the man because he didn't pay his rent.
evade: If you evade something, then you try to avoid it or keep away from it.
eve: The day or night before, usually used for holidays.
My parents always let me open one gift on Christmas Eve.
evacuate: If you evacuate, you leave because of danger.
The firefighters told everyone to evacuate the burning building.
evacuation: Evacuation is the act of evacuating.
There was an emergency evacuation when the fire alarm rang.
evaporate: To evaporate is to turn from liquid into air.
If you leave a pot of water on a hot stove, the water will evaporate.
evocation: An evocation is meant to suggest or bring out something in the imagination.
The calling forth or summoning of a spirit.
The witch's evocation of the evil spirit caused everyone to tremble.
evolutionary: Something that is related to evolution.
Humans have a long and complicated evolutionary history.
everlasting: If something is everlasting then it lasts forever.
evident: If something is evident it is very easy to realize or understand.
It is evident that he is angry by looking at his facial expression.
eventful: If a time or situation was eventful, many important events happen then.
It was an eventful night as he was awarded with the .
evaporation: Evaporation is the process of a liquid converting to the gaseous state.
evoke: If something is being evoked, it is being remember remembered
eviction: An eviction is the action of expelling someone from a property.
eviscerate: If you eviscerate an animal, you remove all of its organs from the animal's body.
evince: If you evince, you show or demonstrate something clearly.
evenly: If something is evenly spread, it is spread out as to form a flat surface.
Spread the icing evenly over the cake.
If you distribute something evenly, you give the same amount of it to everyone.
To avoid arguments, he divided the sweets evenly between his two children.
If a number is evenly divisible, it can be divided to leave no remainder.
evasive: If a person is being evasive, they speak in a way that avoids an issue.
eventuate: If something eventuates, it becomes the result of.
evidently: If something is evidently true or has evidently happened, it is clear or obvious to see.
She was evidently upset by the news.
If something is evidently true or has evidently happened, it seems to be true based on what is known.
Evidently, they forgot to lock the door.
evasion: An evasion is the action of evading something.
